query: For refractory materials, experiments at the solid-to-fluid transition are difficult and yield sparse, scattered data, while the large compositional space of high-entropy systems makes systematic screening impractical. DFT free-energy studies can determine the transition from the crossing of solid and dense-fluid Gibbs energies and provide associated thermodynamic properties, but their reliance on extensive ab initio molecular dynamics makes them costly. TOR-TILD has shown high efficiency for elemental and binary systems, yet becomes substantially slower for multicomponent systems. Any broadly useful approach must retain ab initio-level accuracy, represent all thermodynamic effects identified as important, treat both phases around the transition, and remain practical across relevant compositions and temperatures. For a multicomponent high-entropy material in these high-temperature states, what single intervention could improve determination of transition temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and causal mechanism, its predicted outcome relative to existing experimental and computational baselines, its boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive experiment or benchmark that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Improving the accuracy of thermodynamic databases for high-entropy alloys will enhance the determination of transition temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys in their solid state
generation.mechanism: Improved accuracy of thermodynamic predictions due to better database quality
generation.predicted_outcome: More accurate determination of transition temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity
generation.boundary: High-entropy alloys with complex compositions and high temperatures
generation.uncertainty: The extent to which improved databases will enhance predictions, and potential limitations due to kinetic effects and surface energy

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of thermodynamic predictions using improved and current databases for a set of high-entropy alloys
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the improved database does not result in significantly more accurate predictions than the current database, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Gap and lever. Type: limitation. Statement: The accuracy of thermodynamic predictions is highly dependent on the quality of the databases, which may be incomplete or inaccurate for less studied systems or high temperatures.. System: CrMnFeCoNi High-Entropy Alloy. Lever: database quality. Quote: "Furthermore, the accuracy of all these properties depends highly on the quality of the databases that, in turn, ultimately rely on the available experimental data for optimizing the model parameters and validation."

Gap and lever. Type: limitation. Statement: The current thermodynamic database lacks sufficient accuracy regarding the stability of the L2 1 phase, leading to discrepancies between predicted and observed microstructures.. System: Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti high-entropy alloys. Lever: thermodynamic database stability parameters for L2 1 phase. Quote: "The microstructure discrepancy between the thermodynamic prediction and experimental observation indicates that our current thermodynamic database needs further improvement on the stability of the L2 1 phase."
